- The guarantors of the Senior Notes are not named. The 2024 annual report says certain subsidiaries are not guarantors of the Senior Notes or the Revolving Credit Facility, the 2025 annual report drops that statement, and neither names the guarantors or prints guarantor and non-guarantor financial information. Only the four revolver borrowers are named, so structural priority and asset coverage by entity cannot be established. Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_kalu-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2025-12-31_kalu-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 120

- No credit rating is stated in any filing or in the run settings. Ratings appear only as a factor in financing terms, in the credit thresholds that set derivative collateral for counterparties and in the change-of-control offer to repurchase the 5.875% notes, which applies when the change is accompanied by a ratings decline. Rating-based pricing and triggers cannot be assessed. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_kalu-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 37, 100, 102

- The 2024 annual report and the 2025 annual report give different 2024 amounts because the company changed its inventory valuation method on 2025-01-01. Net income for 2024 is USD 46.8 million in the first and USD 65.7 million as adjusted in the second; Adjusted EBITDA for 2024 is USD 216.5 million in the first and USD 241.0 million as adjusted in the second. Had the former method continued, 2025 would have shown a net loss of USD 29.1 million instead of net income of USD 112.5 million. The 2025 annual report is the later filing and controls FY2025, FY2024 and FY2023; FY2022 exists only in the 2024 annual report on the former method, so any series that reaches back to FY2022 mixes bases. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_kalu-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 58, 116–117; 10-K_2024-12-31_kalu-20241231.htm.jsonl, pages 61, 78

- The three 2026 quarterly reports do not say which inventory method their 2025 comparative figures use, and the 2025 quarterly reports are not supplied. No stand-alone fourth quarter 2025 statement is printed, so it has to be derived from the full year and nine months, and a trailing twelve months figure at 2026-09-30 rests on a nine months 2025 basis that is not confirmed. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 29; 10-K_2025-12-31_kalu-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 58

- Ownership, directors, officers and governance are in the proxy statement, which the annual report incorporates by reference and which is not supplied. Shareholder concentration, board independence and management incentives cannot be described. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_kalu-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 119

- Purchase and capacity commitments are described in words only; no amount is printed in any supplied filing after searching for purchase obligation, purchase commitment, capital commitment and non-cancelable wording. The size of these claims outside debt cannot be stated. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_kalu-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 62

- Nothing dated after the latest quarterly report of 2026-10-22 is supplied: no current report, earnings release or lender presentation. Events between that date and the 2026-11-18 cutoff cannot be checked, and management's outlook is available only as written in the quarterly reports. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 31, 39

facts.label: Leverage and coverage
facts.text: The strongest contrary evidence is that earnings include favorable metal price lag of about USD 63.0 million in the first nine months of 2026 and USD 93.0 million in FY2025, which is 16.63% and 29.98% of issuer Adjusted EBITDA. Third-quarter Adjusted EBITDA was only USD 2.7 million above the prior year and the lag turned unfavorable by about USD 1.0 million, and the issuer now expects full-year Adjusted EBITDA growth toward the lower end of its range. A fall in metal prices would reverse the lag benefit and shrink borrowing-base availability at the same time. Without the trailing twelve months metal price lag of about USD 92.0 million, trailing reported EBITDA would be USD 374.1 million and net leverage 2.46x rather than 1.98x; that is the level the figures support if the lag is treated as non-recurring. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 29, 31; 10-K_2025-12-31_kalu-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 58; calculation CALC-71; calculation CALC-72; calculation CALC-73; calculation CALC-94; calculation CALC-95; calculation CALC-96

facts.label: Cash flow quality
facts.text: Operating cash flow for nine months 2026 is USD 248.1 million against USD 132.0 million a year earlier, but USD 157.2 million of it is a payables increase from higher metal costs and payment timing, set against inventory and receivables builds of USD 123.4 million and USD 108.4 million. Capital expenditure fell to USD 72.2 million from USD 106.4 million, so free cash flow reached USD 175.9 million against USD 25.6 million; on a trailing basis it is USD 124.8 million, after negative free cash flow of USD 25.5 million in FY2025. Dividends of USD 39.2 million were paid in nine months 2026. The issuer's plan of about USD 130.0 million of capital spending for 2026 implies about USD 57.8 million in the fourth quarter against an average of USD 24.07 million a quarter in the first nine months, so nine-month free cash flow overstates the run rate. The payables build is a timing benefit that reverses if metal prices fall or suppliers shorten terms, which would take cash back out of liquidity. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 32; calculation CALC-69; calculation CALC-68; calculation CALC-70; calculation CALC-67; calculation CALC-92; calculation CALC-93

facts.text: Kaiser is a listed, single-segment maker of specialty aluminum mill products with no controlling owner disclosed, so creditors rely on operating cash flow and board discipline, not on sponsor support. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against a benign ownership and event-risk reading is what the filings leave out: holder-level ownership, the party to a director designation agreement that appears in the exhibit lists with dates of 2021 and April 2025, and the guarantor list. A holder with board designation rights, or a large holder pressing for distributions, would raise event risk, and a debt-funded buyback or acquisition would change the view; the USD 93.1 million repurchase authorization has been unused since March 2020 but remains available. Confirmation would come from a proxy statement showing dispersed holders, indentures showing that all material operating subsidiaries guarantee the notes, and renewal of the Richmond contracts without disruption. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against an adequate profile is the earnings run rate: the first half of 2026 carried most of the improvement, third-quarter Adjusted EBITDA grew only 3.32% on net sales growth of 43.98%, and an annualised second half at the low end of the issuer's outlook leaves net debt of USD 921.4 million (USD 934.2 million pro forma for the dividend) at 2.97x, close to 2.96x if EBITDA simply returned to its 2025 level. The nine-month cash flow is also flattered by USD 157.2 million of payables, and a fall in aluminum prices would reverse that build and lower the borrowing base at the same moment, taking liquidity to USD 530.0 million before any base reduction. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest counter-argument is that the earnings improvement is not merely metal: excluding the lag, third-quarter Adjusted EBITDA was 59.47% higher and its margin on conversion revenue rose to 19.36% from 15.20%, packaging conversion revenue per pound rose 17.89%, and capital spending is falling. The view would improve with full-year 2026 free cash flow that stays positive after the payables build unwinds, a fourth quarter near the high end of the outlook, and disclosure that the covenant test is far from its trigger and that guarantors cover the operating subsidiaries. It would weaken with a fourth quarter at or below the low end, loss of one of the two largest customers, a metal price fall that cuts the borrowing base, or a stoppage at the Richmond plant. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 29–31; calculation CALC-2; calculation CALC-7; calculation CALC-15; calculation CALC-17

facts.label: Porter's Five Forces
facts.text: Rivalry is moderate and tied to scale: some competitors for aerospace plate and packaging are substantially larger, and imports and trade orders can alter pricing, so margin cannot be assumed to hold in a downturn. New entrants face multi-year customer qualification and heavy equipment investment, which protects volume, although the filing warns that new parties may qualify. Substitutes matter by end market, with composites and titanium in aircraft, steel in vehicles and glass or plastic in packaging, and a high aluminum price can push customers to switch. Buyer power is the largest force because five customers take 56% of net sales, though long-term agreements and index pricing soften it. Supplier power is moderate: five suppliers provide 82% of primary aluminum and Warrick depends on one party for essential resources, so a supply failure would hit output more than margin. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_kalu-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 25–27, 30, 33–34; 10-K_2025-12-31_kalu-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 116; Business & governance (CP-1A)

facts.label: Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds
facts.text: For the next 12 to 24 months the issuer expects conversion revenue growth toward the high end of 10% to 15% and Adjusted EBITDA growth toward the low end of 45% to 55%, which implies a fourth quarter below the third because of planned outages, execution, customer year-end inventory alignment and metal headwinds, while the coated packaging ramp, aerospace plate volume and lower capital spending are tailwinds and weaker automotive extrusion volume is a headwind. Over three to five years the maturity profile is benign until the revolver in October 2030 and the notes in 2031 and 2034, and refinancing cost will depend on yields that currently value the notes below principal; management's longer-term demand view is stated in its own words and is not tested here. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 31; calculation CALC-4; calculation CALC-13

facts.label: Qualitative downside scenario
facts.text: The initiating condition is a fall in aluminum prices together with customer destocking in aerospace and automotive. The first operational break is metal price lag turning unfavorable and scrap spreads staying tight, which cuts Adjusted EBITDA toward the 2025 level and puts net debt of USD 921.4 million (USD 934.2 million pro forma for the dividend) at 2.96x, or 4.03x at the 2024 level. The financial transmission is a reversal of the USD 157.2 million payables build and falling receivable and inventory values, which lowers the borrowing base and takes liquidity from USD 687.2 million to USD 530.0 million before any base reduction; trailing cover would still be 5.83x at the 2025 EBITDA level. Management can cut capital spending below the USD 130.0 million plan, suspend the dividend of about USD 12.8 million a quarter and draw the undrawn revolver, and no principal is due before October 2030, so resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress. The first observable signals would be fourth-quarter Adjusted EBITDA below USD 70.99 million, a fall in the Midwest Transaction Price and renewed revolver borrowing. Primary downside path: a metal price fall that reverses working capital and shrinks the borrowing base while earnings return to the 2025 level. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 31–32; 10-K_2025-12-31_kalu-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 35; calculation CALC-5; calculation CALC-12

facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Kaiser presents an adequate business profile supported by liquidity, a long maturity runway, pass-through pricing and a recovery in underlying earnings, but credit quality is constrained by customer concentration, metal and working capital timing, unproven free cash flow and slowing quarterly earnings. Cash-flow durability appears adequate rather than strong because trailing free cash flow of USD 124.8 million rests on lower capital spending and a payables build. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on aluminum prices through the borrowing base, on the cost of refinancing the 2031 and 2034 notes and on covenant terms not supplied. The primary downside path is a metal price fall with customer destocking that reverses working capital and returns earnings to the 2025 level, which would raise net leverage to 2.96x while liquidity stays ample. Further analysis would require the credit agreement, the indentures, the proxy statement, peer data and the fourth-quarter result. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: metal price timing and customer concentration. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-5; calculation CALC-10; calculation CALC-12

No output of another module is an input to this module.
## Findings
### Bottom line

The five supplied filings, the latest for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, support the requested credit snapshot of Kaiser Aluminum Corp with limitations, so creditors can rely on reported debt, liquidity and earnings but not on covenant headroom, guarantor coverage or ratings.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 14–15, 29, 31; calculation CALC-2; calculation CALC-5

Three limits shape how far the figures can be used. The 2025 annual report adjusts 2024 and 2023 for an inventory accounting change, so the 2024 annual report is not comparable for those years. The quarterly reports do not state the inventory basis of their 2025 comparatives. The credit agreement and indentures are not supplied, so the level of the springing fixed charge coverage test and the list of guarantors are not established.

## Gaps

- Covenant terms are not established. No supplied filing prints the level of the springing fixed charge coverage test, the availability level that switches it on, or any indenture covenant level, and the credit agreement and indentures are not supplied. Every filing was searched for fixed charge coverage, availability threshold, financial covenant, springing and ratio-level wording; management says only that it does not expect to trigger the test in the next 12 months. Covenant headroom cannot be calculated and the legal and covenant analysis cannot run.

- The guarantors of the Senior Notes are not named. The 2024 annual report says certain subsidiaries are not guarantors of the Senior Notes or the Revolving Credit Facility, the 2025 annual report drops that statement, and neither names the guarantors or prints guarantor and non-guarantor financial information. Only the four revolver borrowers are named, so structural priority and asset coverage by entity cannot be established.

- No credit rating is stated in any filing or in the run settings. Ratings appear only as a factor in financing terms, in the credit thresholds that set derivative collateral for counterparties and in the change-of-control offer to repurchase the 5.875% notes, which applies when the change is accompanied by a ratings decline. Rating-based pricing and triggers cannot be assessed.

- The 2024 annual report and the 2025 annual report give different 2024 amounts because the company changed its inventory valuation method on 2025-01-01. Net income for 2024 is USD 46.8 million in the first and USD 65.7 million as adjusted in the second; Adjusted EBITDA for 2024 is USD 216.5 million in the first and USD 241.0 million as adjusted in the second. Had the former method continued, 2025 would have shown a net loss of USD 29.1 million instead of net income of USD 112.5 million. The 2025 annual report is the later filing and controls FY2025, FY2024 and FY2023; FY2022 exists only in the 2024 annual report on the former method, so any series that reaches back to FY2022 mixes bases.

- The three 2026 quarterly reports do not say which inventory method their 2025 comparative figures use, and the 2025 quarterly reports are not supplied. No stand-alone fourth quarter 2025 statement is printed, so it has to be derived from the full year and nine months, and a trailing twelve months figure at 2026-09-30 rests on a nine months 2025 basis that is not confirmed.

- Ownership, directors, officers and governance are in the proxy statement, which the annual report incorporates by reference and which is not supplied. Shareholder concentration, board independence and management incentives cannot be described.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_kalu-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 119

- Purchase and capacity commitments are described in words only; no amount is printed in any supplied filing after searching for purchase obligation, purchase commitment, capital commitment and non-cancelable wording. The size of these claims outside debt cannot be stated.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_kalu-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 62

- Nothing dated after the latest quarterly report of 2026-10-22 is supplied: no current report, earnings release or lender presentation. Events between that date and the 2026-11-18 cutoff cannot be checked, and management's outlook is available only as written in the quarterly reports.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 31, 39

## Findings
### Bottom line

Net debt is 1.98x trailing reported EBITDA at September 30, 2026 and liquidity is USD 687.2 million, so creditors have no near-term refinancing pressure, but the earnings recovery leans on metal price timing and a USD 157.2 million payables build.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 14, 29, 31; calculation CALC-30; calculation CALC-56; calculation CALC-86

The covenant test level is not stated, so headroom cannot be measured, and the 2024 annual report is not comparable with later periods for 2024 and 2023.

### Leverage and coverage

Net debt fell from USD 1,052.6 million at 2025-12-31 to USD 921.4 million at 2026-09-30 while trailing reported EBITDA rose from USD 311.3 million to USD 466.1 million, so net leverage dropped from 3.38x to 1.98x. About 1.12x of that fall comes from higher EBITDA and 0.28x from lower net debt, which is cash build rather than repayment because gross debt moved only from USD 1,059.6 million to USD 1,038.7 million. Cash interest paid over the trailing twelve months is USD 53.4 million, which gives cover of 8.73x, up from 6.21x in FY2025 and 5.64x in FY2024.

The strongest contrary evidence is that earnings include favorable metal price lag of about USD 63.0 million in the first nine months of 2026 and USD 93.0 million in FY2025, which is 16.63% and 29.98% of issuer Adjusted EBITDA. Third-quarter Adjusted EBITDA was only USD 2.7 million above the prior year and the lag turned unfavorable by about USD 1.0 million, and the issuer now expects full-year Adjusted EBITDA growth toward the lower end of its range. A fall in metal prices would reverse the lag benefit and shrink borrowing-base availability at the same time. Without the trailing twelve months metal price lag of about USD 92.0 million, trailing reported EBITDA would be USD 374.1 million and net leverage 2.46x rather than 1.98x; that is the level the figures support if the lag is treated as non-recurring.

### Cash flow quality

Operating cash flow for nine months 2026 is USD 248.1 million against USD 132.0 million a year earlier, but USD 157.2 million of it is a payables increase from higher metal costs and payment timing, set against inventory and receivables builds of USD 123.4 million and USD 108.4 million. Capital expenditure fell to USD 72.2 million from USD 106.4 million, so free cash flow reached USD 175.9 million against USD 25.6 million; on a trailing basis it is USD 124.8 million, after negative free cash flow of USD 25.5 million in FY2025. Dividends of USD 39.2 million were paid in nine months 2026. The issuer's plan of about USD 130.0 million of capital spending for 2026 implies about USD 57.8 million in the fourth quarter against an average of USD 24.07 million a quarter in the first nine months, so nine-month free cash flow overstates the run rate. The payables build is a timing benefit that reverses if metal prices fall or suppliers shorten terms, which would take cash back out of liquidity.

### Liquidity and maturities

Liquidity is USD 687.2 million: cash of USD 117.3 million plus USD 569.9 million of revolver availability after USD 5.1 million of letters of credit, up from USD 547.2 million at 2025-12-31. Restricted cash of USD 19.6 million is excluded. The revolver commitment of USD 575.0 million is undrawn and matures in October 2030, the 4.50% notes of USD 550.0 million fall due in June 2031 and the 5.875% notes of USD 500.0 million in March 2034, so no principal is due before 2030. The revolver is limited by a borrowing base of eligible receivables and inventory, so availability depends on metal prices and working capital.

## Gaps

- High: covenant headroom is not calculable. No supplied filing prints the level of the springing fixed charge coverage test or the availability that switches it on, and the credit agreement is not supplied; management states only that it does not expect to trigger the test in the next 12 months. Obtaining the credit agreement would close this.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32

- Medium: the 2024 and 2023 amounts in the 2024 annual report are on the former inventory method and differ from the adjusted amounts in the 2025 annual report (net income for 2024 of USD 46.8 million against USD 65.7 million; Adjusted EBITDA of USD 216.5 million against USD 241.0 million). The 2025 annual report is used. FY2022 exists only on the former method, no FY2023 balance sheet is printed on the new method and FY2023 Adjusted EBITDA on the new method is not stated, so FY2023 leverage and FY2023 Adjusted EBITDA are not supplied. A FY2023 balance sheet and an Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation for FY2023 on the weighted average cost basis would close this.

- Medium: the three 2026 quarterly reports do not state the inventory method of their 2025 comparatives and the 2025 quarterly reports are not supplied, so every trailing twelve months figure rests on a 2025 comparative basis that is not confirmed. The 2025 quarterly reports or a statement of the comparative basis would close this.

- Medium: the guarantors of the Senior Notes, the ranking of the notes against the revolver and the indenture covenants are not stated, so the debt stack ranks the notes below the secured revolver only on the stated security. The indentures would close this.

- Medium: no stand-alone fourth quarter 2025 statement is printed. Q4 2025 net sales, reported EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA are calculated as full year less nine months and labelled calculated; other Q4 2025 lines are not supplied.

- Medium: the issuer's share of net sales under supply chain financing (about 31% in Q3 2026 and 32% in FY2025) cannot be rebuilt from the receivables sold printed (USD 362.1 million in Q3 2026 against net sales of USD 1,214.5 million), and the programmes are off balance sheet. The programme documents would close this.

- Low: the filings print a dash, which the method treats as missing, for these lines and periods: Restructuring costs in Q1 2026, Q2 2026, H1 2026, Q3 2025, Q3 2026, 9M 2026; Other operating charges, net in FY2023, FY2025, Q3 2025, 9M 2025; Deferred tax assets, net in Q1 2026, Q2 2026, Q3 2026; Non-cash asset impairment charge in FY2023, H1 2025, 9M 2025; (Gain) loss on disposition of property, plant and equipment in Q1 2025; Bad debt expense in FY2023, H1 2025; Annual variable cash contributions to Salaried VEBA in FY2023; Proceeds from sale of equity securities in H1 2026, 9M 2026; Borrowings under the Revolving Credit Facility in FY2024; Repayment of borrowings under the Revolving Credit Facility in FY2024; Issuance of 5.875% Senior Notes in FY2023, FY2024; Repayment of principal of 4.625% Senior Notes in FY2023, FY2024; Cash paid for debt issuance costs in FY2023, FY2024. Each is shown as not supplied rather than zero. The issuer's own reconciliations treat most of them as nil.

- Low: the issuer prints no gross profit, so it is calculated before depreciation and amortization, and trade and other receivables are printed separately only in the annual report. Lines that a filing does not print at all are shown as not supplied for its periods, including the other operating charges line in the first and second quarter reports and several cash flow lines in the quarterly reports; the Q2 and Q3 discrete cash flow columns are not printed because the quarterly reports give cumulative cash flows only.

- Low: purchase and capacity commitments are described without amounts, so claims outside debt are incomplete; lease liabilities of USD 26.5 million (operating) and USD 14.7 million (finance) at 2025-12-31 and the pension and retiree medical liability of USD 72.1 million at 2026-09-30 are excluded from Total Debt.

- Low: the maturity ladder is derived from instrument maturity dates because the quarterly reports refer to the 2025 annual report for maturities; that report prints a dash for 2026 to 2029, USD 22.3 million for 2030 (the revolver, since repaid) and USD 1,050.0 million thereafter. The note maturity days are stated only for the 2034 notes; the 2031 notes are dated by month.
- Low: no segment profit is disclosed because there is one reportable segment; revenue by end market is shown in the KPI table and the end-market lines sum to consolidated Net sales.

spans.text: ## Request

Kaiser Aluminum Corp (issuer kalu-811596), as of 2026-11-18, pathway credit snapshot. Scope: business, ownership, governance, transaction and corporate-structure facts from the five supplied filings, covering 2024 to the quarter ended 2026-09-30. No acquisition or sponsor transaction is supplied; the transactions covered are the 2025 refinancing, the revolver amendment and one asset exit.
## Sources

| Source readiness (CP-0) | 6637bb26bcc1403d3cd5c5dd708e7d71971c23fa4f0755d6b3fb76449d6337f9 | Source set, version relationship between the two annual reports, and the gaps for the proxy statement, guarantors and covenant levels |
## Findings
### Bottom line

Kaiser is a listed, single-segment maker of specialty aluminum mill products with no controlling owner disclosed, so creditors rely on operating cash flow and board discipline, not on sponsor support. The only recent financing transactions were an amount-neutral refinancing of the 2028 notes into notes due 2034 and a revolver extension to October 2030, which pushed maturities out but raised the coupon on the refinanced amount by 1.25 percentage points.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_kalu-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 53, 77; 10-K_2025-12-31_kalu-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 102, 104; calculation CALC-15

Holder-level ownership, board independence and guarantor coverage are not established because the proxy statement and the indentures are not supplied, so the ranking of the notes against subsidiary creditors cannot be assessed here.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_kalu-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 119–120; Source readiness (CP-0)
### Key findings

Conversion revenue is a better gauge of the business than net sales: net sales rose 46.40% in the nine months of 2026 while conversion revenue, the part left after metal cost, rose 17.68%, so most of the growth is metal pass-through that enlarges receivables and inventory rather than margin.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 26, 30; calculation CALC-8

Packaging is the largest line by sales but contributes less to margin than its sales share suggests: it is 45.84% of nine-month 2026 net sales and 39.95% of conversion revenue, while aerospace plate is 24.71% of net sales and 31.00% of conversion revenue.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 26, 30; calculation CALC-3; calculation CALC-6

Customer concentration is the main business risk: the two largest customers took 31% of 2025 net sales and the five largest 56%, and the annual report says losing the largest could have a material adverse effect.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_kalu-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 30, 116; calculation CALC-10

Metal-price neutrality is substantial but incomplete: firm-price sales exposed the company on 11.43% of 2025 shipments by weight, and alloy cost pass-through can lag, so earnings still swing with metal timing.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_kalu-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; calculation CALC-11

Customer supply chain financing makes cash conversion depend on customers: receivables transferred under customer programs equalled 32% of 2025 net sales and 31% of third-quarter 2026 net sales, and they sit outside reported debt.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_kalu-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; calculation CALC-22

No sponsor or controlling holder appears in the evidence supplied, which lowers event risk from a financial sponsor, though holder concentration is untested: the stock is listed on Nasdaq and a classified board is led by a combined chairman and chief executive.

Distributions are steady and moderate against earnings, but cash cover is not yet proven: operating cash flow covered capital spending plus dividends only 0.59x in 2025, and the 2.23x cover in the nine months of 2026 was helped by a USD 157.2 million build in accounts payable.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_kalu-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 76; 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5–6, 32; calculation CALC-17

Creditor access to subsidiary assets is not established: the company is a holding company over wholly owned operating subsidiaries, four of which are revolver borrowers, the notes carry guarantors named only in the indentures, and the warning in the 2024 annual report that certain subsidiaries are not guarantors is absent from later reports.

Labor exposure is concentrated near the as-of date: about 65% of employees are unionized, the Richmond contracts expire in November 2026, and the 2026 quarterly reports are silent on the earlier 2026 renewals, while the Trentwood and Newark contracts run to September 2030.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_kalu-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 21, 39; calculation CALC-13

Warrick, the largest plant by floor area, is a single point of dependence: it is the dedicated packaging site and relies on Alcoa for essential resources such as potable water, under agreements whose terms are not supplied.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a benign ownership and event-risk reading is what the filings leave out: holder-level ownership, the party to a director designation agreement that appears in the exhibit lists with dates of 2021 and April 2025, and the guarantor list. A holder with board designation rights, or a large holder pressing for distributions, would raise event risk, and a debt-funded buyback or acquisition would change the view; the USD 93.1 million repurchase authorization has been unused since March 2020 but remains available.

The strongest operating counterpoint is that the 2026 recovery is real but partly metal-driven: shipments rose 7.94% and conversion revenue per pound rose, yet net sales grew far faster than conversion revenue, so a fall in metal prices would reverse part of the working capital build. Loss of one of the two largest customers, which hold 31% of net sales, or a stoppage at Richmond or another plant would also weaken the view. Confirmation would come from a proxy statement showing dispersed holders, indentures showing that all material operating subsidiaries guarantee the notes, and renewal of the Richmond contracts without disruption.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 26, 30; calculation CALC-8; calculation CALC-10
### Limitations

- The no-sponsor reading rests on cover-page share counts and the number of record holders; beneficial-owner percentages, director independence and related-party dealings sit in a proxy statement that is not supplied, so a single large holder would overturn it.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_kalu-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 119

- The statement that creditors may rank behind subsidiary creditors rests on one risk-factor paragraph in the 2024 annual report, because the guarantor lists are named only in documents not supplied; full guarantee coverage would remove this concern.
- Customer shares are as printed for 2025 only; contract terms, expiry dates and customer names are not supplied, so the concentration conclusion cannot say how soon revenue is at risk.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_kalu-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 30, 116
- Labor conclusions stop at the contract expiry dates printed at 2025-12-31; renewal outcomes in 2026 are not stated, so the Richmond expiry in November 2026 is shown as unresolved.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_kalu-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 21
- The dividend declared on 2026-10-13 is shown as scheduled for 2026-11-13 because no filing after 2026-10-22 is supplied, so distributions after the latest report are not confirmed.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

Kaiser's only financing transactions in the period were completed in the fourth quarter of 2025. In November 2025 it issued USD 500.0 million of unsecured senior notes due 2034-03-01 at par and redeemed in full the USD 500.0 million of unsecured notes due March 2028 at 100% of principal, funded by the new notes, cash on hand and revolver borrowings; USD 2.1 million of unamortized issuance costs on the old notes was written off. The new notes carry a coupon 1.25 percentage points above the old notes, which adds USD 6.25 million of annual interest on the same amount, and the maturity moves out by 6 years. The company may be required to offer to repurchase the new notes on certain asset sales or on a change of control accompanied by a ratings decline.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_kalu-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 102–103; calculation CALC-15

In October 2025 the asset-based revolver was amended to mature in October 2030 with a maximum commitment of USD 575.0 million, of which up to USD 50.0 million may be used for letters of credit, and an accordion of USD 200.0 million plus a first-in last-out tranche. The amount that can be borrowed is set by eligible receivables, inventory and certain other assets, which secure the revolver. In the nine months of 2026 the company borrowed USD 397.8 million and repaid USD 420.1 million, including the USD 22.3 million drawn at 2025-12-31, and no borrowings were outstanding at 2026-09-30 or 2026-10-19; total liquidity was USD 687.2 million at 2026-09-30. Senior notes principal is USD 1,050.0 million, made up of the 4.50% notes due June 2031 and the notes due 2034.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_kalu-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 104; 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 31–32; calculation CALC-16

No acquisition, sponsor transaction or business combination is described as occurring in 2024, 2025 or 2026 in the five filings; the filings refer to two earlier acquisitions, Warrick, which closed on 2021-03-31, and Imperial Machine & Tool Co., whose date is not stated. The Sherman, Texas extrusion facility, which was being exited from the second quarter of 2024, was sold in the fourth quarter of 2025 at a charge of USD 7.5 million; sale proceeds are not stated. Quarterly dividends of USD 0.77 per share, about USD 12.8 million each, were declared on 2026-04-13, 2026-07-13 and 2026-10-13, with the last expected to be paid on or about 2026-11-13; payment is not confirmed in any supplied filing.

spans.text: ## Request

Kaiser Aluminum Corp (issuer kalu-811596), as of 2026-11-18, pathway credit snapshot. Scope: the fundamental credit profile built from the five supplied filings and the accepted outputs on source readiness, financial foundation and business and governance, covering the period to 2026-09-30. No rating, security recommendation, legal-capacity conclusion or recovery view is given.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| 10-K_2025-12-31_kalu-20251231.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025 | 2026-02-19 | b62b8e5845803734cb3a820beea90aae00900af2adf100f816d48ad030f83019 | Risk factors, cost structure, conversion revenue and Adjusted EBITDA, liquidity, debt note, customers and capital spending |

| 10-Q_2026-03-31_kalu-20260331.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2026 | 2026-04-23 | e7d286164afff0508ca04c0cff08ac10ced9d7ad3a101045f60563c50628fc2b | Fixed charge coverage statement and revolver position at 2026-04-20 |

| 10-Q_2026-06-30_kalu-20260630.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 | 2026-07-23 | bca45827b9fe8071fcc99ce881bdeaabdd29be0d8cce3ae913e98a205b3384d8 | Fixed charge coverage statement and revolver position at 2026-07-20 |

Upstream module outputs supplied to this module:
| Module | sha256 | Use |

| Source readiness (CP-0) | 6637bb26bcc1403d3cd5c5dd708e7d71971c23fa4f0755d6b3fb76449d6337f9 | Source set, version relationship between the two annual reports and the gaps for covenant levels, guarantors and ratings |

| Financial foundation (CP-1) | f044278b9c81852c0817bb12eb4f877ce9b78bdb4e5c5180c56097231129bc8d | Net debt, trailing reported EBITDA, leverage, cover, free cash flow, liquidity, claims outside debt and the pro forma adjustment for the dividend declared 2026-10-13 |

## Findings
### Bottom line

Kaiser's fundamental credit profile is adequate: trailing net leverage of 1.98x (2.00x pro forma for the dividend declared on 2026-10-13) and no maturity before October 2030 limit near-term refinancing risk, but earnings have slowed since the first half.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14–15, 31; calculation CALC-1

Third-quarter Adjusted EBITDA was USD 84.0 million against an average of USD 147.4 million a quarter in the first half, and an outlook at the low end of the issuer's range implies leverage near 2.97x on the second-half run rate. Customer concentration, metal price timing and covenant and guarantor terms that are not supplied keep the view at adequate.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 29, 31; calculation CALC-3; calculation CALC-4; Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Key findings

Deleveraging is real and mostly earnings-driven: net debt of USD 921.4 million (USD 934.2 million pro forma for the dividend) is 1.98x trailing EBITDA (2.00x pro forma) against 3.38x at 2025-12-31, a fall of 1.40x of which 1.12x came from higher EBITDA and only 0.28x from lower net debt.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-1

Underlying earnings improved by more than the metal price lag explains: Adjusted EBITDA excluding the favorable lag was USD 315.8 million in the nine months of 2026 against USD 158.4 million a year earlier, and the lag's share of Adjusted EBITDA fell from 28.78% to 16.63%.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; calculation CALC-2

Momentum is slowing and the trailing figures flatter the run rate: Adjusted EBITDA fell from an average of USD 147.4 million a quarter in the first half to USD 84.0 million in the third quarter, and the outlook, which the issuer now places toward the low end of 45% to 55% growth, implies about USD 70.99 million in the fourth quarter if it lands at 45%, which puts leverage at 2.97x on the second-half run rate before the dividend.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 29, 31; calculation CALC-3; calculation CALC-4

Free cash flow is the least proven dimension: it was USD -13.7 million in FY2024 and USD -25.5 million in FY2025 and reached USD 124.8 million on a trailing basis only after capital spending fell and USD 157.2 million of payables built, so cash conversion has not been shown through a metal price cycle.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; calculation CALC-10; calculation CALC-20

Business risk is moderate and customer-led: packaging is 39.95% and aerospace plate 31.00% of nine-month 2026 conversion revenue, but the two largest customers take 31% of net sales and the five largest 56%, so one contract loss would move earnings more than any single end-market cycle.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_kalu-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 30, 116; calculation CALC-14; calculation CALC-17

Margin resilience rests on pass-through pricing, not cost flexibility: metal is 65.51% of 2025 cost of products sold and is passed to customers, yet Adjusted EBITDA over conversion revenue moved from 16.55% in FY2024 to 21.35% in FY2025, 29.58% in nine months 2026 and 19.13% in the third quarter, because metal lag, scrap spreads and plant outages drive much of the swing.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_kalu-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 56, 58–59; 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 29–30; calculation CALC-6; calculation CALC-9

Liquidity and the maturity profile are the strongest supports: liquidity of USD 687.2 million is 12.87x trailing cash interest, the revolver is undrawn, and no principal falls due before the revolver matures in October 2030 and the 2031 notes follow, although availability depends on receivable and inventory values that fall with metal prices.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14–15, 31; 10-K_2025-12-31_kalu-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 35; calculation CALC-12

Capital markets access looks adequate but not cheap: the notes due 2031 and 2034 carry fair values of 91.80% and 93.46% of principal at 2026-09-30, so refinancing at current yields would cost more than the coupons, a matter for 2030 and later rather than now.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; calculation CALC-13

Financial policy is moderate so far: dividends took 20.60% of nine-month 2026 net income, repurchases have been suspended since March 2020 and capital spending is falling, but the incentive plan names no leverage or cash flow measure and the board is led by a combined chairman and chief executive.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-19

Structural and covenant questions are open and bound the view: the guarantor list, the level of the fixed charge coverage test that applies only below an availability threshold, and credit ratings are not supplied, so conclusions rest on reported figures.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against an adequate profile is the earnings run rate: the first half of 2026 carried most of the improvement, third-quarter Adjusted EBITDA grew only 3.32% on net sales growth of 43.98%, and an annualised second half at the low end of the issuer's outlook leaves net debt of USD 921.4 million (USD 934.2 million pro forma for the dividend) at 2.97x, close to 2.96x if EBITDA simply returned to its 2025 level. The nine-month cash flow is also flattered by USD 157.2 million of payables, and a fall in aluminum prices would reverse that build and lower the borrowing base at the same moment, taking liquidity to USD 530.0 million before any base reduction.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 29, 32; 10-K_2025-12-31_kalu-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 35; calculation CALC-4; calculation CALC-5; calculation CALC-8; calculation CALC-12

The strongest counter-argument is that the earnings improvement is not merely metal: excluding the lag, third-quarter Adjusted EBITDA was 59.47% higher and its margin on conversion revenue rose to 19.36% from 15.20%, packaging conversion revenue per pound rose 17.89%, and capital spending is falling. The view would improve with full-year 2026 free cash flow that stays positive after the payables build unwinds, a fourth quarter near the high end of the outlook, and disclosure that the covenant test is far from its trigger and that guarantors cover the operating subsidiaries. It would weaken with a fourth quarter at or below the low end, loss of one of the two largest customers, a metal price fall that cuts the borrowing base, or a stoppage at the Richmond plant.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 29–31; calculation CALC-2; calculation CALC-7; calculation CALC-15; calculation CALC-17

### Strengths and weaknesses

The first strength is liquidity and a clear maturity runway: liquidity of USD 687.2 million, an undrawn revolver and no principal due before October 2030 mean a metal price shock or a customer stoppage would be absorbed before it became a refinancing problem, which supports a low near-term default pathway and gives management room to wait out the cycle.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14–15, 31; calculation CALC-12

The second strength is the earnings recovery beyond metal lag: Adjusted EBITDA excluding lag nearly doubled in the nine months of 2026 and net leverage fell by 1.40x, so debt service capacity is stronger than a year ago and trailing cover of 8.73x on cash interest gives wide room, although the run rate is below the trailing figure.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-1; calculation CALC-2; calculation CALC-5

The third strength is pass-through pricing: index and spot pricing pass aluminum and alloy cost to customers, firm-price sales are only 11.43% of shipments, and packaging conversion revenue per pound rose 17.89%, so the business earns on conversion rather than on metal and most price swings do not reach EBITDA, except through lag and scrap spreads.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_kalu-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 30; calculation CALC-15; calculation CALC-16

The fourth strength is a qualified position that is hard to enter: suppliers must pass rigorous qualification, some packaging approvals take multiple years, and the company has added capacity at Trentwood and a coating line at Warrick, so the recovery in volume after the 2025 outage has a barrier against new entrants and supports revenue durability.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_kalu-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 64; Business & governance (CP-1A)

The fifth strength is moderate financial policy: repurchases are suspended, dividends are 20.60% of nine-month net income and capital spending is falling toward USD 130.0 million for 2026, so cash is not being diverted from debt service and leverage tolerance appears conservative, though no leverage target is stated.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 34–35; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-19

The first weakness is customer concentration: the two largest customers take 31% of net sales and the five largest 56%, so loss or repricing of one contract would remove volume from plants with substantial fixed costs and cut EBITDA faster than any end-market cycle, and no contract terms are supplied.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_kalu-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 30, 116; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-17

The second weakness is exposure to metal price timing and working capital: favorable lag was 16.63% of nine-month Adjusted EBITDA, payables built by USD 157.2 million, and receivables sold under customer programs rose 33.98%, so a price fall would reverse earnings and cash flow while shrinking the borrowing base that supports liquidity.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18, 29, 32; 10-K_2025-12-31_kalu-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 35; calculation CALC-2; calculation CALC-12

The third weakness is unproven free cash flow: free cash flow was negative in FY2024 and FY2025 and capital spending ran at 1.12x depreciation in FY2025, so the trailing positive figure depends on lower capital spending and a payables build and may not persist at the planned fourth-quarter spending of USD 57.8 million.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; calculation CALC-10; calculation CALC-11

The fourth weakness is margin volatility and the third-quarter slowdown: Adjusted EBITDA over conversion revenue fell to 19.13% in the third quarter from 29.58% in the nine months, with scrap spreads, the Bellwood outage and coating line ramp-up named as causes, so the improved margins of 2026 are not yet a stable base.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 29–30; calculation CALC-6; calculation CALC-8

The fifth weakness is opacity of the creditor position: guarantors, the fixed charge coverage trigger level and ratings are not supplied, a combined chairman and chief executive leads the board, and the incentive plan names no leverage measure, so creditors cannot test structural ranking or covenant headroom.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0); Business & governance (CP-1A)

### Company description

Kaiser is a single-segment producer of semi-fabricated specialty aluminum mill products, and its revenue splits over four cyclical end markets in which packaging is the largest by sales and aerospace plate the second-largest contributor to conversion revenue. About 70% of shipments go directly to manufacturers and tier one suppliers, mostly under long-term agreements with metal pass-through pricing, so volume is reasonably visible while margin visibility depends on a few large contracts and on metal timing; debt service capacity therefore rests on conversion revenue, not on net sales.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_kalu-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 16; calculation CALC-14
### Ownership and group structure

Kaiser is a Nasdaq-listed holding company with no sponsor or controlling holder stated, operating through wholly owned subsidiaries of which four borrow under the revolver; holder-level ownership and the guarantor list are not supplied. The board is classified and chaired by the chief executive, and the incentive plan rewards total shareholder return and Adjusted EBITDA margin, so financial discipline rests on policy choices already visible: repurchases suspended since March 2020 and dividends at 20.60% of nine-month net income.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 35; calculation CALC-19
### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Volume and mix, not price, drive earned revenue: shipments rose 7.94% in the nine months of 2026 and conversion revenue per pound rose to USD 1.42 from USD 1.30, while net sales grew 46.40% on metal pass-through and conversion revenue only 17.68%. Firm-price sales are 11.43% of 2025 shipments, so pricing power shows in conversion margin rather than in net sales, and packaging conversion revenue per pound rose 17.89% as coated products ramped. Demand is cyclical in aerospace and automotive, concentrated in a few customers and exposed to substitution by composites, steel and plastics, according to the risk factors.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 26, 30; 10-K_2025-12-31_kalu-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 16, 26–27; calculation CALC-14; calculation CALC-15; calculation CALC-16
### Cost structure and margin resilience

Metal is 65.51% of 2025 cost of products sold and passes through to customers, leaving non-metal costs of USD 1,010.8 million (34.49%) made up of manufacturing 23.70%, plant overhead 6.19%, freight 2.87% and other 1.73%, with a high share of fixed cost in packaging that makes margin depend on plant utilization. Operating leverage cut both ways: in 2025 lower volume and start-up costs were outweighed by favorable metal consumption cost and mix, and in the third quarter of 2026 net sales grew 43.98% but Adjusted EBITDA only 3.32% because of lower scrap utilization, tighter scrap spreads, planned outages and freight, so margins can be defended against metal but not against operating deleverage.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_kalu-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 27, 56, 59; 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 29–30; calculation CALC-8; calculation CALC-9
### Capital intensity and cash flow conversion

EBITDA has converted weakly into free cash flow: capital spending was 9.42% of conversion revenue and 1.12x depreciation in FY2025, free cash flow was -5.99% and -8.19% of reported EBITDA in FY2024 and FY2025, and the trailing 26.78% follows lower capital spending and a net working capital outflow of USD 74.6 million that is helped by the payables build. Capital spending is discretionary and the plan of USD 130.0 million implies USD 57.8 million in the fourth quarter, so flexibility exists if volumes weaken; leases, pension and retiree obligations and the environmental accrual sit outside debt but are small beside it, according to Financial foundation.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 32, 34; calculation CALC-10; calculation CALC-11; calculation CALC-20
### Porter's Five Forces

Rivalry is moderate and tied to scale: some competitors for aerospace plate and packaging are substantially larger, and imports and trade orders can alter pricing, so margin cannot be assumed to hold in a downturn. New entrants face multi-year customer qualification and heavy equipment investment, which protects volume, although the filing warns that new parties may qualify. Substitutes matter by end market, with composites and titanium in aircraft, steel in vehicles and glass or plastic in packaging, and a high aluminum price can push customers to switch. Buyer power is the largest force because five customers take 56% of net sales, though long-term agreements and index pricing soften it. Supplier power is moderate: five suppliers provide 82% of primary aluminum and Warrick depends on one party for essential resources, so a supply failure would hit output more than margin.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_kalu-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 25–27, 30, 33–34; 10-K_2025-12-31_kalu-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 116; Business & governance (CP-1A)
### PEST factors

Trade policy is material to credit because the filing lists duties and tariffs among the drivers of primary aluminum pricing, and the Midwest premium rose from USD 0.19 to USD 0.59 per pound, which with the LME price lifted the average to USD 1.78 in 2025 from USD 1.29 in 2024, up 37.98%; that inflates receivables, inventory and the borrowing base on the way up and reverses on the way down. Fuel-efficiency standards and defense budgets move aerospace and automotive demand, and sustainability preferences support aluminum packaging, but the filings give no quantified effect, so these are monitored rather than weighted.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_kalu-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 15, 28–29, 34; calculation CALC-18
### Credit-translated SWOT

The credit strengths are liquidity with a long maturity runway, earnings recovery beyond metal lag, pass-through pricing, qualification barriers and moderate financial policy; the weaknesses are customer concentration, metal and working capital timing, unproven free cash flow, margin volatility and an opaque creditor position. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are the coated packaging ramp, aerospace plate volume on the added Trentwood capacity and lower capital spending; threats are a metal price fall that shrinks the borrowing base, a customer loss, a plant stoppage and refinancing at higher yields after 2030.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-12; calculation CALC-13; calculation CALC-15
### Financial profile and credit quality

The nine dimensions assess as follows. Scale and market position is average, with USD 3,373.0 million of 2025 net sales but larger competitors. Competitive advantage is average, resting on qualification barriers and coated packaging capability. Business diversification is average because four end markets are offset by customer concentration. Cost and capex flexibility is average, since metal passes through and capital spending is discretionary but fixed costs are high in packaging. Margin stability is weak, with the margin on conversion revenue ranging from 16.55% to 29.58% across comparable periods. Free cash flow stability is weak, with negative free cash flow in FY2024 and FY2025. Ability to refinance and access capital markets is average, with no maturity before October 2030 but notes valued below principal. Liquidity position is strong at USD 687.2 million, subject to the borrowing base. Financial policy and governance is average, with moderate distributions offset by open structural and covenant terms.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 31; calculation CALC-6; calculation CALC-10; calculation CALC-12; calculation CALC-13
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

For the next 12 to 24 months the issuer expects conversion revenue growth toward the high end of 10% to 15% and Adjusted EBITDA growth toward the low end of 45% to 55%, which implies a fourth quarter below the third because of planned outages, execution, customer year-end inventory alignment and metal headwinds, while the coated packaging ramp, aerospace plate volume and lower capital spending are tailwinds and weaker automotive extrusion volume is a headwind. Over three to five years the maturity profile is benign until the revolver in October 2030 and the notes in 2031 and 2034, and refinancing cost will depend on yields that currently value the notes below principal; management's longer-term demand view is stated in its own words and is not tested here.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 31; calculation CALC-4; calculation CALC-13
### Qualitative downside scenario

The initiating condition is a fall in aluminum prices together with customer destocking in aerospace and automotive. The first operational break is metal price lag turning unfavorable and scrap spreads staying tight, which cuts Adjusted EBITDA toward the 2025 level and puts net debt of USD 921.4 million (USD 934.2 million pro forma for the dividend) at 2.96x, or 4.03x at the 2024 level. The financial transmission is a reversal of the USD 157.2 million payables build and falling receivable and inventory values, which lowers the borrowing base and takes liquidity from USD 687.2 million to USD 530.0 million before any base reduction; trailing cover would still be 5.83x at the 2025 EBITDA level. Management can cut capital spending below the USD 130.0 million plan, suspend the dividend of about USD 12.8 million a quarter and draw the undrawn revolver, and no principal is due before October 2030, so resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress. The first observable signals would be fourth-quarter Adjusted EBITDA below USD 70.99 million, a fall in the Midwest Transaction Price and renewed revolver borrowing. Primary downside path: a metal price fall that reverses working capital and shrinks the borrowing base while earnings return to the 2025 level.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kalu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 31–32; 10-K_2025-12-31_kalu-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 35; calculation CALC-5; calculation CALC-12
### Overall credit view

Overall, Kaiser presents an adequate business profile supported by liquidity, a long maturity runway, pass-through pricing and a recovery in underlying earnings, but credit quality is constrained by customer concentration, metal and working capital timing, unproven free cash flow and slowing quarterly earnings. Cash-flow durability appears adequate rather than strong because trailing free cash flow of USD 124.8 million rests on lower capital spending and a payables build. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on aluminum prices through the borrowing base, on the cost of refinancing the 2031 and 2034 notes and on covenant terms not supplied. The primary downside path is a metal price fall with customer destocking that reverses working capital and returns earnings to the 2025 level, which would raise net leverage to 2.96x while liquidity stays ample. Further analysis would require the credit agreement, the indentures, the proxy statement, peer data and the fourth-quarter result. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: metal price timing and customer concentration.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-5; calculation CALC-10; calculation CALC-12
